steps.title: Open the app's home page
steps.narration: Let's start by opening the dashboard and checking the app's status.
steps.point_out: The green Ready pill in the top-right corner indicates the app is connected to the backend.

steps.title: Check the freshness indicator on the badge
steps.narration: Next to the Ready pill, there's a small gray text showing how fresh this status reading is. This is new.
steps.point_out: Look for the 'as of Ns ago' text right next to the Ready badge. It tells you how many seconds old this status information is.

steps.title: See the freshness note on the confirmation strip
steps.narration: Below the top bar is a green strip confirming the board is current. It also shows the same freshness note.
steps.point_out: The preflight banner reads 'GO — today's board is current. (as of Ns ago)' — the staleness note is now on this strip too.

steps.title: Refresh the page to see the status update live
steps.narration: Reload the page. You'll see the Ready pill and staleness text reappear instantly, showing it's a live reading each time.
steps.point_out: The badge and staleness text don't freeze — they refresh on every page load.

steps.title: Navigate to the backtest page
steps.narration: Let's go to the backtest section to see the scorecard table. Click the Backtest link in the sidebar.
steps.point_out: The sidebar has a link to Backtest. This page shows forward-looking return metrics in a scorecard.

steps.title: View the scorecard table with return horizons
steps.narration: The scorecard shows forward returns for different time horizons: 1-day, 5-day, 10-day, 20-day, and 60-day.
steps.point_out: Each row in the table represents one horizon. The numbers show the median return (or '—' if the horizon hasn't elapsed yet).

steps.title: Navigate to a historical date to see background compute
steps.narration: Click the left arrow next to the date selector to step back to a previous historical date. This may trigger background computation.
steps.point_out: When a compute window is active, a chip appears in the top bar saying 'background compute running (N)'. With this update, the Ready badge stays visible alongside it, even at narrow window widths.
